messages:
sam-sales: Heads-up — AuroraHealth procurement just sent back the order form with three redlines: Net-60 payment terms, an SLA availability tweak, and a DPA subprocessor carveout. They also asked for a PO number to be included before signature. Can we confirm: 1) POC credit still valid if we sign with Net-60? 2) Signature routing path (multiple signers on their side)? 3) Any compliance blockers for the DPA change?
maria-ps: Thanks for flagging. POC credit was approved for up to $12k for this pilot but finance needs invoice timing clarified if Net-60. If we accept Net-60 we can still honor the credit, but we need a billing contact and an expected invoice date. Who at Aurora is handling billing?
taylor-finance: @maria-ps FYI — Net-60 okay for enterprise, but we need an internal PO match and their vendor onboarding timeline. If the PO will arrive after service start, we usually ask for a billing contact and to note invoice will be issued at activation. Can we put that in the order form: "Invoice @ activation; payment due Net-60 from invoice date"?
kevin-legal: Can y'all drop the redlines here? quick read: the SLA tweak — is it availability percentage or remedies? The subprocessor carveout in the DPA often needs a mapping of subprocessors + KMS/HSM requirements. If they want unlimited subprocessors with approval rights, that's a no from our standard DPA.
sam-sales: Pasted the three snippets they sent (copied from email):
```
1) Payment terms: "Customer to pay within 60 days of invoice. Invoice to include PO# when provided."
2) SLA change: "Availability commitment adjusted to 99.5% with credit of 5% monthly pro rata for downtime exceeding 0.5%"
3) DPA change: "Customer requires prior written approval for any subprocessor engagements, plus right to audit subprocessors."
```
maria-ps: Ok on the payment snippet — sounds usual. For the SLA, 99.5% is lower than our standard 99.9 for dedicated customers; offering 99.5 with a small credit is plausible for a short POC but engineering/ops should confirm we can support fallback. @linh-eng, can runtime tolerate the paperwork to accept a 99.5 pledge for this pilot?
linh-eng: Quick check: POC will run on shared hosted capacity (not dedicated). We can't guarantee 99.9 on hosted for extended runs; 99.5 is safer to promise for a 30-day pilot. However, the wording about automatic credits needs to be limited: propose caps and a timeboxed SLA for pilot only. Also want to avoid punitive language that affects rollout. Suggest: "99.5% availability for the pilot period only; remedies capped at 10% of the pilot fees."
kevin-legal: Agree with @linh-eng. For the DPA subprocessor ask — we can provide a list of subprocessors and offer notice; we can't do prior approval for every subprocessor (operationally impossible). Propose counter-language: "Customer will be notified of material changes to subprocessors and may object to a new subprocessor within 30 days for reasonable security grounds." Also push back on audit rights — we can offer SOC report or third-party attestation in lieu of full audit.
sam-sales: Nice. So action items: (1) confirm billing contact for invoice timing (maria/taylor), (2) draft counterlanguage for SLA + DPA (kevin/linh), (3) agree signature path — Aurora has two signers (legal + procurement) and wants doc signed via DocuSign. I can route but need exact signers.
maria-ps: I have a contact: rachel.kim@aurorahealth.org — procurement. I'll confirm PO lead and expected PO date.
taylor-finance: Once you have PO lead, finance can accept Net-60 and queue invoice on activation. We'll add the text: "Invoice issued at activation; payment due Net-60 from invoice date. Invoice will include PO number if provided."
kevin-legal: Draft counterlanguage we should send: 
```
SLA (pilot only): Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% availability during the pilot period. Remedies for unavailability during the pilot are limited to a credit not to exceed 10% of fees paid under the pilot. This pilot SLA expires at the end of the pilot term.
DPA (subprocessors): Provider may engage subprocessors for the provision of services. Provider will maintain a list of current subprocessors and will notify Customer of material changes. Customer may object to a new subprocessor within 30 days on reasonable security grounds. Provider will provide third-party security attestation (e.g., SOC 2) upon request in lieu of on-site audits.
```
sam-sales: That reads clean. I'll send it back as a tracked redline. Question on signature routing: Aurora wants both procurement and legal to sign; do we need an exec signature?
maria-ps: For POC order forms we usually need procurement + legal only. Exec sign usually for larger committed contracts.
linh-eng: Also note: if they require KMS/HSM for key management in the DPA, that adds lead time — not for pilot typically. Ask them if they actually require customer-managed keys or just stronger data-at-rest wording.
sam-sales: Good call. I'll ask: "Do you require customer-managed keys or is enhanced encryption/attestation sufficient?"
contract-bot: Document uploaded: /files/aurora/orderform_2026-03-18.pdf (uploaded by sam-sales)
kevin-legal: Please also attach their redline PDF (we need to mark changes). Once I get their exact DPA lines, I can produce a tracked counter to send back.
maria-ps: I confirmed billing contact: rachel.kim@aurorahealth.org. She says PO expected in ~3 weeks after vendor onboarding. She asked if service can start earlier of we sign — we answered yes but invoice will be dated at activation.
taylor-finance: Good — we can accept that. Finance will annotate the order form with the invoice language and queue payment terms.
sam-sales: Plan: I'll reply to Aurora with: (a) counter SLA + DPA language above, (b) confirm Net-60 invoice at activation, (c) request exact signers and whether DocuSign is fine, (d) question on KMS requirement. Will loop in @kevin-legal when they send the redline PDF.
kevin-legal: Sounds good. If they insist on prior approval for subprocessors we'll escalate but try the 30-day objection path first. Also capture that remedies cap for pilot only.
linh-eng: One more technical note — if they request logs retention >90 days or additional PCI-level controls, that will require an infra review. Ask them to confirm retention requirements now so we don't get surprised.
sam-sales: Will ask. I'll post their redline when it lands. Thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin-legal: :eyes: awaiting redline
maria-ps: :+1:
